Author: Rajeev Singh
Bench: Rajeev Singh
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench

Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 678 of 2023
Applicant :- Pankaj Soni
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Deptt. Of Home Lko.

Heard Shri C.B. Pandey learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and learned counsel appearing for the complainant.

The present bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant seeking anticipatory bail in F.I.R. No. 005 of 2023, under Sections 504, 506, 376, 323 I.P.C., Police Station Bazarkhala, District Lucknow.

In pursuance of the earlier order, Mr. Ramesh Chand Yadav, Investigating Officer/S.H.O., P.S.
Bazar Khala, District Lucknow is present.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant has falsely been implicated in the present case.

It is further submitted that as per prosecution case, the incident was taken place six Pankaj Soni vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Deptt. Of ... on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90689722/
1 years ago when the victim was minor and now the victim is doing LL.B.

sentences.text: It is vehemently submitted that no date and time of the the alleged incident is mentioned in the F.I.R. and only general allegations have been levelled.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that as a matter of fact,
monetary help was always given by the applicant to the informant and her family members with the assurance that the money will be refunded to him.

Drawing the attention of the Court towards Annexure 4 to the application, learned counsel for the applicant submits that on different dates, the money was given to the informant and her family members.
However, when the said money was demanded back by the applicant, the F.I.R. has been lodged on the basis of concocted facts.
It is also submitted that all the photographs annexed with the supplementary affidavit (at page 11) were taken by some other persons in presence of the parents of the victim as well as informant.
It is next submitted that the statements of the victim have already been recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. and there is no possibility of tampering of any evidence.

Learned counsel for the applicant,
while assuring that the applicant will cooperate in the investigation, submits that the applicant does not have any criminal antecedent and the police is trying to arrest in the present case.
In such circumstances, applicant is entitled for protection of this Court under the provisions of anticipatory bail.

Learned A.G.A. as well as learned counsel for the complainant oppose the prayer of the applicant and submit that victim has categorically supported the prosecution story, as the applicant is trying to blackmail by saying that he will air all the photographs of the victim or she has to live with the applicant as a 'keep'.
It is, thus, submitted that the application is liable to be rejected.
However, the informant, who is present before this Court, admits that the aforesaid photos were taken in her presence.

I have considered the argument of the learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. as well as learned counsel for the complainant and gone through the contents of the F.I.R., bail application and other relevant records, including the case diary.
The case diary placed by the Investigating Officer before this Court reveals that statements of the victim have been recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.

In her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the victim stated that six years ago, when she was studying in Class 10, she was allured by the applicant and he made physical relations with the victim.
Thereafter, in the year 2020, the applicant again made physical relations with her.

She further stated that the applicant started demanding Rs.20 lac and gave threat that, in case, the amount is not paid to him, he will air all the photographs and videos, those were taken by the applicant with her.

In her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., she stated that six years ago, she met with the applicant in a marriage and thereafter he started visiting her house and she was having fatherly feeling with the applicant.
She further stated that one day, when nobody was in the house, the applicant made physical relations with her and also clicked photos of her.
She also stated that thereafter, she was being blackmailed and now the applicant is demanding Rs.20 lacs since three months ago from the date of lodging of the F.I.R.
However, in the statements recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. nor 164 Cr.P.C., the date or time of the incident has not been disclosed by the victim.

It is also evident from the record that money was Pankaj Soni vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Deptt. Of ... on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90689722/
2 given to the family members of the victim by the applicant.
Keeping in view the reasons, as stated above , a case for interim bail to the applicant is made out.
Thus, having regard to all the facts and circumstances of the case, the present anticipatory bail application stands finally disposed of with the direction that till the submission of the police report,
if any, under Section 173(2) Cr.P.C. before the competent court, in the event of arrest of the applicant- Pankaj Soni, involved in aforesaid F.I.R., he shall be released on anticipatory bail on his furnishing personal bond of Rs.20,000/- with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Station House Officer of the police station concerned with the following conditions:-
(1) The applicant shall make himself available for interrogation or for discovery of any fact by a police officer/investigating officer as and when required and will cooperate in the investigation.

sentences.text: (2) The applicant shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer;
(3) The applicant shall not leave the country without the previous permission of the Court.
(4) The applicant shall deposit his passport with the trial court and if he has not been issued any passport, an affidavit in this regard shall be filed by him before the trial court.
Any violation of above conditions will be treated misuse of bail and court below will be at liberty to pass appropriate order in the matter.
